title: Teaching jobs in Vietnam: where to find them (2026)
description: Where Vietnam teaching jobs are really posted, when Saigon schools hire, applying from abroad or in person, recruiters, and a week-by-week search plan.
h1: Finding a teaching job in Vietnam: where to look, when to apply and a weekly plan
intro: Most English teaching jobs in Vietnam are advertised by the employers themselves on their careers sites, on teaching job boards and in Facebook groups; international schools recruit through group portals and international boards. Language centres in Ho Chi Minh City hire all year, busiest from June to August and quietest from mid-December to Tet. Apply to several direct channels at once, never pay anyone to be hired, and do not teach a class until your work permit is issued.
keyPoints: Go direct first: the big chains (VUS, ILA, Apollo, British Council) recruit through their own careers sites, and the big international schools through group portals and international boards such as Schrole and TES.

Centres hire all year; the busiest stretch is June to August and the quietest is mid-December to Tet (Saturday 6 February 2027). For public-school agency jobs, apply in June–August for a September start.

**Never pay to be hired.** VUS says any request for money is a scam and VAS says it never charges recruitment fees; since 10 September 2026 a school or company that takes a deposit or keeps your original documents is fined {{vnd:40000000-50000000}}.
In July–October 2026 job ads, Ho Chi Minh City centres offered {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour, most new-teacher offers {{vnd:430000-560000}}. 'Up to' rates are ceilings, not your pay.
You can interview from abroad with the big employers, but you may not teach a paid class before your work permit is issued: the worker's fine is {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and you can be deported.

sections.title: Where teaching jobs in Vietnam are advertised

blocks.text: Ho Chi Minh City is the country's biggest market: in August 2025 it had [1,961 licensed foreign-language and IT centres](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-nang-cao-chat-luong-nhan-su-tai-cac-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-10388655.html), 158 of them foreign-invested, plus international and bilingual schools, public-school programmes staffed through education companies, kindergartens and universities. Each kind of employer advertises in its own places, so the channel you use decides which jobs you see. If you are not yet sure which kind of job you want, read [the types of teaching jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/types-of-english-teaching-jobs-in-vietnam) first.

blocks.text: Employers' careers pages

The large chains publish their vacancies and hiring steps themselves: VUS at [teachenglish.vus.edu.vn](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/?p=979), Apollo English at [apollo.edu.vn/teach](https://apollo.edu.vn/teach), and ILA at teachingenglish.ila.edu.vn. British Council posts appear irregularly under About > Jobs on [britishcouncil.vn](https://www.britishcouncil.vn/en/about/jobs/senior-teaching-assistant-hcmc-2026), and the HCMC posts found in 2026 were teaching-assistant roles. International schools mostly hire through their group portals: ISHCMC through [Cognita Careers](https://www.ishcmc.com/who-we-are/careers/), with academic roles also on Schrole and TES, and BIS HCMC through the [Nord Anglia portal](https://www.nordangliaeducation.com/bis-hcmc/careers). If that is your target, read [international school jobs in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/international-school-jobs-in-vietnam).
Job boards

Vietnam Teaching Jobs, run from Da Nang, is free for teachers to join and also sells paid document and work-permit services; its ads are also posted on Teast. ESLbase and TEFL.org carry ads from the chains too, and say they do not verify employers' claims. Treat every board ad as a lead: check the deadline, then apply through the employer's own site or email where you can.
Facebook groups

Teachers commonly use expat and teacher Facebook groups to hear about jobs and to ask about schools; we could not verify which groups are active and moderated in 2026. Groups are also where fake recruiters work: scammers copy real schools' names, logos and contact details. Only answer posts you can trace back to an employer's own website, and move the conversation to that employer's official email.
eno.vn

eno.vn's [teaching jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) gathers postings from job boards and schools' careers pages; a linked posting opens the original ad, where you apply, and expires within 14 days. eno.vn has not verified the employers behind them and does not handle applications. [The school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City employers (language centres, international and bilingual schools, universities and teacher agencies), with open jobs and a place where teachers who worked or interviewed there can vote and leave reviews (read by a moderator before they appear); most schools have few or no reviews yet. A free teacher profile, started at [teacher.eno.vn](https://teacher.eno.vn), lets schools and centres find you: anyone signed in to eno.vn can message you, and your phone number, email and CV stay hidden until you choose to share them in that chat.
Job sites side by side, as checked on 19 October 2026

We checked each site on 19 October 2026, on its own pages where it let us read them. Treat the counts as a snapshot: ads come and go every day, each site counts in its own way, and three sites blocked our check, so they have no figure. The sites are listed in no order of preference.

sections.title: When schools hire, and how long a search takes

blocks.text: Language centres hire all year, but demand peaks before and during the summer holiday. Public schools finish before 31 May and return in late August, and IELTS centres [report enrolment peaking in July and August](https://tienphong.vn/bo-cong-diem-chung-chi-ielts-mieng-banh-nghin-ti-se-ra-sao-post1879043.tpo). Teachers report the slowest stretch as mid-December to Tet, which falls on Saturday 6 February 2027. Plan your search around those dates rather than the calendar year.

blocks.caption: When each type of employer hires in Ho Chi Minh City (job ads and the 2026–27 school calendar, as of October 2026)
rows: Language centres
All year; busiest June–August
Hiring is slowest from mid-December to Tet. As of October 2026 the chains were still advertising: ILA had separate postings for overseas and in-country applicants open to 31 December 2026.
Public-school programmes via agencies
June–August for a September start; some openings around semester 2 in January
The 2026–27 school year opened on 5 September 2026 and ends before 31 May 2027; contracts follow it (for example September to May).
International schools
Well ahead of the next school year
Sources disagree on the exact cycle. Teachers commonly advise having your teaching licence, references and recruiter profiles ready by September–October for the following August.
Universities and the British Council
When posts open; British Council vacancies appear irregularly
Expect to need a CELTA or equivalent; universities also want experience: RMIT's 2026 Educator role asks for at least 3 years' post-CELTA experience.

blocks.text: The school year dates come from [HCMC's 2026–27 calendar](https://giaoduc.net.vn/tphcm-ban-hanh-ke-hoach-thoi-gian-nam-hoc-2026-2027-post262099.gd). The hiring step itself can be quick: VUS, for example, runs an online form and documents, then a video interview of about an hour. The slow part is the paperwork. Documents from abroad have to be apostilled or legalised and translated, the employer then files the work permit 60 to 10 days before your start date, and the decision takes up to 10 working days under the decree (the city publishes 5). Gathering documents from abroad typically takes weeks to months, so start them before you start applying.

Hourly-paid teachers also start slowly: teachers report that hours build up over the first weeks and that the first payday can come about a month after you start. Teachers commonly advise bringing enough money for 2 to 3 months without full pay; the [eno.vn Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) shows median asking rents by district to help you size it.

sections.title: Applying from abroad or looking on the ground

blocks.text: Both work, and the right choice depends on which employers you want. Most language-centre interviews in Vietnam happen in person, but the big employers interview overseas candidates by video: VUS holds video interviews with HR, and [VAS](https://vas.edu.vn/en/news/vietnam-australia-international-school-vas-warning-about-fraudulent-recruitment-information) prefers in-person interviews but uses Teams or Zoom for overseas candidates. Some public-school agency ads require proof that you are already in Vietnam.

blocks.text: What has to be ready before you fly

Whichever route you take, documents issued abroad must be prepared in the country that issued them. Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention with effect from 11 September 2026 (Decree 293/2026/ND-CP): documents from member countries need an [apostille](https://www.hcch.net/en/instruments/conventions/status-table/?cid=41), while documents from Germany, Austria and Czechia, which objected, from Thailand until 28 February 2027, and from non-member countries still need consular legalisation. Your criminal record must be issued no more than 6 months before the employer files, so time it carefully; the health check is in practice done in Vietnam. The details are in [getting your degree authenticated](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-your-degree-authenticated-for-vietnam).

Teachers are filed as 'experts' under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025: a bachelor's degree or higher plus at least 2 years of relevant work experience, usually proved by a letter from a past employer abroad. For experts in education, the decree also lists documents showing you meet the education-law qualification standard as an alternative proof, but how Ho Chi Minh City applies that to a teacher with under 2 years' experience is not published. If that is you, ask each employer which proof they will file and get the answer in writing before you travel. Never use an experience letter that is not true: an employer filing altered or forged documents is fined {{vnd:40000000-60000000}} ({{vnd:80000000-120000000}} for a company, school or centre).

Your employer arranges the rest of your paperwork once your work permit is issued; ask them exactly what they cover and what it costs. The full procedure is in [the work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers).

sections.title: Recruiters and agencies: what they do and who pays

blocks.text: 'Agency' means three different things in Vietnam's teaching market, and the money flows differently in each.

items: **Recruiters** find candidates for schools and pass them to the employer, which then hires you directly. A legitimate recruiter's fee should come from the school, not from you. We found no published legal cap on fees charged to job-seekers, so the safe rule is simply to refuse any fee.

**Public-school agencies** are education companies that employ you and place you in public schools; examples in 2026–27 ads include DTP Education Solutions, GEMS and EMG Education. The agency is your employer and holds your contract and work permit. DTP's and GEMS's 2026–27 ads offered about {{vnd:430000-550000}} an hour on weekday daytime schedules, September to May.

**Placement programmes and 'TEFL plus job' packages** sell a course with a job attached. A programme may charge for the course, but a fee for the job itself is the warning sign described in [teaching job scams](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam); before paying for any package, get the full cost, the employer's name and the work-permit plan in writing. Check the course itself as you would any TEFL: [how to check a TEFL course before you pay](/teach-in-vietnam/tefl-tesol-and-celta-for-vietnam#accreditation-red-flags). Packages aimed at people without a degree cannot fix the law: the expert route needs a university degree.

blocks.title: Never pay to get a job
blocks.text: The most common way a search goes wrong is a fee. [VUS warns](https://teachenglish.vus.edu.vn/fake-job-warning) that applying is free and that any request for money or to download an app is a scam; VAS says it never charges recruitment, training or entrance fees and never asks candidates to open e-wallets. An employer may not take a deposit or keep your original passport, degree or certificates ([Labour Code Art. 17](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html)); since 10 September 2026 a company or school that does is fined {{vnd:40000000-50000000}} and must return them. More warning signs are in [teaching job scams in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam).

Two questions to put to any public-school agency. First, is the hourly rate before or after its cut? One 2026 job-board guide reports agencies deducting 5 to 10% from salaries, though no agency publishes this. Second, is your work permit issued before you start? An [HCMC education department directive](https://voh.com.vn/giao-duc/trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tai-tphcm-khong-duoc-thu-hoc-phi-dai-han-510985.html) requires centres sending teachers into schools to show each teacher's work permit first, and since January 2026 schools running linked programmes [must hold a full file for each foreign teacher](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-ra-soat-nang-luc-bang-cap-giao-vien-chuong-trinh-lien-ket-10402625.html), with no documents accepted after signing.

Check every recruiter's email against the employer's own domain: genuine VUS recruitment emails end in @vus-etsc.edu.vn, VAS emails in @vas.edu.vn and ILA's recruitment address is at @ilavietnam.edu.vn. A request for ID numbers, bank details or document photos through an unofficial channel, a request to install an app, or a link to buy your flight through the recruiter are reasons to stop.

sections.title: Checking an employer before you say yes

blocks.text: Centres open and close quickly: in the 2025–26 school year Ho Chi Minh City [dissolved or revoked 112 language and IT centres](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/ho-chi-minh-city-shuts-down-112-language-and-it-centers-2556885.html). Old guides and job boards still list employers that no longer exist: ACET [closed on 31 December 2024](https://www.idp.com/vietnam/blog/official-acet-announcement/?lang=en), Apax Leaders [collapsed owing wages](https://vietnamfinance.vn/he-thong-te-liet-va-giai-the-apax-leaders-dang-no-ca-tram-ty-dong-d108066.html), and American International School Vietnam [was dissolved in January 2026](https://tuoitre.vn/nld/american-international-school-officially-dissolved-196260114102410854.htm) and ordered to settle the salaries and insurance owed to its staff. So check before you accept.

Confirm the legal entity and its city licence, ask current teachers whether pay has been on time, check where the campus really is (since 1 July 2025 an 'HCMC' job can be in former Binh Duong or Ba Ria-Vung Tau, and official addresses use new ward names while ads still say District 1 or Binh Thanh), and get the guaranteed hours, gross or net pay and who pays each paperwork step in writing; the city's fee for a new work permit is {{vnd:600000}}, paid by the employer. The full check, with the red flags, is in [how to check an employer before you sign](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-job-scams-in-vietnam#how-to-check-an-employer), and the contract terms are in the [contracts guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teaching-contracts-in-vietnam).

Do not teach before the permit is issued, even during a 'trial month'. Under [Decree 283/2026/ND-CP](https://news.tuoitre.vn/foreign-workers-in-vietnam-what-to-know-as-new-penalty-rules-take-effect-september-10-103260824152235374.htm), from 10 September 2026, working without a permit costs the worker {{vnd:15000000-25000000}} and can lead to deportation. In Ho Chi Minh City the Department of Home Affairs issues permits for practically every language centre and school ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html), 21 September 2026), and a permit is tied to one employer: changing schools, or adding a second one, needs a new permit. Your employer and the authority have the final word on your case.

sections.title: A week-by-week plan for the search

blocks.text: This plan assumes you have a degree and a TEFL, TESOL or CELTA and want a language-centre or public-school job in Ho Chi Minh City. International-school candidates should start months earlier. If you are still getting the certificate or the documents together, start with [the steps to becoming an English teacher in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/how-to-become-an-english-teacher-in-vietnam).

items.title: Before week 1: start the documents
items.text: Order your degree apostille or legalisation and collect signed experience letters from past employers abroad (dates, role, hours, on letterhead). Leave the criminal record check until it will still be under 6 months old on the filing date.

items.title: Week 1: get findable
items.text: Update your CV and record a short intro video (VUS asks non-native speakers for one). Create your free profile at [teacher.eno.vn](https://teacher.eno.vn), and draw up a shortlist of 10 to 15 employers from careers pages and [the school directory](/schools). Our [CV and demo lesson guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-cv-and-demo-lesson-in-vietnam) shows what Saigon employers look for.

items.title: Week 2: apply direct
items.text: Apply through the careers pages of your shortlist first, then to board ads you can trace back to a real employer. Join two or three teacher Facebook groups and note who posts regularly. Keep a simple tracker: employer, date applied, contact, next step.

items.title: Week 3: interviews and demo lessons
items.text: Before each demo lesson, ask who will watch, the learners' age and level and how long it runs. A demo is part of the interview, not paid teaching: a paid class before your permit is issued is work without one. Bring a printed plan and a backup in case no students are present.

items.title: Week 4: check and compare offers
items.text: For each offer, talk to current teachers, confirm the work location and get hours, pay basis and paperwork costs in writing. Compare offers on guaranteed monthly income, not the 'up to' hourly rate; the [salary guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam) shows what is normal.

items.title: Weeks 5–6: accept and file
items.text: Accept the offer in writing (pay, hours and start date), read the draft contract, hand over certified copies rather than originals, and agree the start date so the employer can file your work permit 60 to 10 days ahead. The labour contract itself is signed once the permit is issued, before you start. If no offer has come yet, widen the net: part-time posts, kindergartens, agency jobs or a second city.

blocks.text: Once applications are out, keep a weekly rhythm rather than refreshing boards every hour:

blocks.caption: A weekly routine during an active search (suggested schedule)
rows: Monday
Check careers pages and job boards for new ads; eno.vn's linked postings expire within 14 days, so check weekly
Tuesday
Send 3 to 5 tailored applications; follow up on any older than a week
Wednesday
Research the employers that replied: licence, location, current teachers
Thursday
Interviews and demo lessons; prepare plans the evening before
Friday
Update your tracker and documents; reply to every message within a day

faqs.q: Can non-native English speakers find teaching jobs in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Yes, though it takes more applications. Decree 219 sets no native-speaker or nationality condition for a work permit, but at language centres Circular 21/2018 asks non-native teachers for more, for example proof of level 5 (about C1) English plus a teaching certificate. Nationality lists in ads are employer preferences: VUS considers non-native speakers who send an intro video, and RMIT accepts non-natives with IELTS Academic 8.0 (no band below 7.5).

faqs.q: Can I find a teaching job in Vietnam without a degree?
faqs.a: Not a legal one. The expert route that teachers use requires a bachelor's degree or higher, and working without a work permit means a fine and possible deportation. Be wary of any package that promises a job without one.

faqs.q: Is a TEFL certificate enough, or do I need a CELTA?
faqs.a: Most centres accept an accredited TEFL or TESOL of 120 hours or more, which is an employer convention rather than a legal minimum. Universities and the British Council usually ask for a CELTA or equivalent, and a TEFL never replaces the degree, and on its own it does not replace the experience in the work-permit test.

faqs.q: Can I teach at two schools at the same time?
faqs.a: Only if each employer holds a work permit for you. A permit is tied to the employer, so a second school needs its own permit, and teaching there without one is treated as working without a permit.

faqs.q: Will Vietnam's plan to make English a second language create more jobs for foreign teachers?
faqs.a: Possibly, but slowly. Decision 2371/QD-TTg (October 2025) mainly trains and recruits Vietnamese teachers and only orders research into letting foreigners teach in public schools. Ho Chi Minh City is piloting 246 schools that may contract foreign teachers directly from 2026 to 2030, but no such ads had appeared by October 2026.

faqs.q: Are ACET and Apax Leaders still hiring?
faqs.a: No. ACET stopped operating in Vietnam on 31 December 2024, and the Apax Leaders chain collapsed in 2023–24 owing teachers' wages and insurance, after which the city suspended its centres. Ignore old ads that still list them.
